title: Give each price-feed subscription its own off switch

blocks.text: A trading screen is made of widgets: charts, tickers, a blotter. Each one subscribes to a symbol's prices on `PriceFeed` when the trader opens it, usually with a lambda or a method reference, and closes what `subscribe` returned when the trader closes it. The blotter subscribes the same listener to several symbols.

Finish `subscribe(String symbol, DoubleConsumer listener)` in `src/main/java/practice/PriceFeed.java`. It registers the listener for that symbol and returns a `Subscription`; closing that subscription stops exactly that registration, whatever else the same listener or the same symbol is subscribed to, and lets the feed forget it. `tick` and the `Entry` class are written. About three lines in total.

cases.says: an open subscription hears every price of its symbol and none of other symbols
after its subscription is closed a widget hears no more prices and the feed no longer holds it
closing one subscription of a listener subscribed to two symbols leaves the other subscription working
closing one widget's subscription leaves other widgets on the same symbol subscribed
when the same listener is subscribed twice to one symbol, closing one subscription, even twice, leaves the other working

origin.section: A Listener Is Removed by the Reference It Was Added With, and a Second Lambda Is Another Object

concepts: A subscribe that returns a handle owning its own entry removes exactly that registration on close, even when the same listener is subscribed more than once.
